description.value: Free Spirit Spheres is a world-renowned treehouse resort on Vancouver Island featuring three handcrafted spherical treehouses suspended among coastal rainforest trees near Qualicum Bay. The adult-only property sits on a 5-acre forested lot with a central pond, shared bathhouse with sauna, and a galley kitchen — a glamping experience marketed as among the most unique accommodations in the world. It could serve as an exotic overnight base for cyclists exploring Vancouver Island's interior and nearby Horne Lake area.

address.value: 420 Horne Lake Rd, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1Z7, Canada

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content is rich and confirms an active, operating treehouse glamping resort. Guest Services page explicitly states 'We do not provide breakfast' (false for that amenity) and confirms WiFi ('There is also WiFi on the property'). No mention of bike storage, bike procedures, laundry, e-bike charging, or any cycling-specific amenities anywhere on the site, so those remain null per absence-of-evidence rules. Contact page corroborates OSM phone and address (with a fuller postal address), confirming those fields.
concerns: OSM address ('420 Horne Lake Road') lacks city and postal code; website contact page provides fuller address '420 Horne Lake Rd, Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 1Z7, Canada' — used website version.
Property is marketed as 'adult only' — may exclude family touring cyclists.
No mention of bike storage, secure bike facilities, or any cycling-specific services anywhere on the website.
OSM tags the property as tourism=hotel, but it is a boutique glamping treehouse resort — minor categorization nuance, not a material concern.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a legitimate, operating accommodation but it is an adult-only glamping property with no mention of any bike storage or cycling-specific facilities; both required WWC criteria are unconfirmed. It may appeal to adventure-seeking touring cyclists as a destination stay, but lacks the baseline bike-handling infrastructure typically expected for WWC inclusion.
enrichment_extras.notes: The spheres are small suspended treehouses (e.g., Eryn is 10.5ft diameter); storing touring bikes or loaded panniers inside a sphere is implausible. Secure external bike storage would be the relevant question for a follow-up inquiry.
